questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

Have the toys been put away by the children?

options.text: Has the children put away the toys?
Did the children put away the toys?
Have the children put away the toys?
Had the children put away the toys?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Have the children put away the toys?**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Whenever we change from active to the passive form we use the general order as 'Object+ Auxillary verb+Past participle+by+Subject'.
 
• Here, the verb used is 'have' which is used for 'toys', in passive voice will remain 'have' for the plural object 'children'.
 
• In an interrogative sentence, the verbs like Has, Have, Had, Will, Shall, Can, May etc, do not change their position at the beginning of the sentence while changing the sentence from Active to Passive voice
 
• For e.g.- Had she finished the assignment? [Active voice]

​ Had the work been finished by him? [Passive voice]

The correct solution-* Have the children put away the toys?*

questions.question:
Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement required, select "No improvement".

I have__ the good news__ for you.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. good news .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"news"** is an **uncountable noun** in English, even though it ends in 's'.
 
• Uncountable nouns cannot be used with indefinite articles like **"a"** or **"an"**, nor do they typically take a definite article **"the"** unless referring to specific, previously mentioned information.
 
• When introducing information for the first time, we simply use the noun without an article or use a phrase like **"some news"** or **"a piece of news."**
 
• In this context, **"good news"** is the most natural and grammatically correct way to improve the sentence.

Correct sentence: *I have **good news** for you.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Why other options are incorrect__**

 
• **Option 1 ("no any good news"):** This is a **double negative/redundancy** error. You can say "no good news" or "not any good news," but "no any" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 2 ("an good news"):** This is incorrect because **"news"** is uncountable and cannot take the article "an." Additionally, "an" is only used before vowel sounds; "good" starts with a consonant sound.
 
• **Option 4 ("No improvement"):** The original **"the good news"** implies that the listener already knows which news is being discussed. Since the sentence is usually used to introduce new information, "good news" is the better general choice.

questions.question:
Given below are four sentences, three of which, are jumbled. Pick the option that gives the correct order.

A. If you had been away from the planet for the past quarter of a century, one of the few things you might find comfortingly familiar on your return is the world of sport.

B. While the digital revolution has transformed the way we shop, chat, date, do politics and consume culture, sport looks largely unchanged.

C. There hasn't been a major new sport invented for more than a century.

D. From football to cricket to golf. it's still the same old staples, hitting a ball into a hole or goal or over a boundary.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __ABCD__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**1.**Here we need an introductory line for the paragraph, B,C,and D doesn't fit to such requirement they are not an independent statement.Hence we left with only A-If you had been away from the planet for the past quarter of a century, one of the few things you might find comfortingly familiar on your return is the world of sport.

**2**.B and C are dependent on each other, it is conveying that there hasn't been much change in sport world while digital world has changed a lot. So B is the most suitable fit.

**3**.C will be followed by B.

**4**.we only left with D and is the most opt line to be the **concluding statement.**

**Hence the complete paragraph will be- **

*If you had been away from the planet for the past quarter of a century, one of the few things you might find comfortingly familiar on your return is the world of sport.While the digital revolution has transformed the way we shop, chat, date, do politics and consume culture, sport looks largely unchanged. There hasn't been a major new sport invented for more than a century. From football to cricket to golf. it's still the same old staples, hitting a ball into a hole or goal or over a boundary.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four sentences, three of which, are jumbled. Pick the option that gives the correct order.**

A. Tailor birds make beautiful nests.

B. Then she sews the thread through a leaf to make a secure nest for her eggs.

C. Each stitch is neat and precise so that the leaf can be prevented from ripping.

D. In order to make a nest, the bird looks for a thread made of cotton or wool.
questions.solution:
The correct sequence for the given sentences is 'ADBC'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sentence A comes first as it states the subject 'Tailor birds'
 
• Sentence D follows A as it states what these birds look for to make a nest.
 
• Sentence B follows D as it tells how the nest is made through leaves.
 
• Sentence C follows B as it concludes why the nest is woven precisely.
 
• Thus, the sequence becomes:
 
 
• A: Tailor birds make beautiful nests.​
 
• D: In order to make a nest, the bird looks for a thread made of cotton or wool.
 
• B: Then she sews the thread through a leaf to make a secure nest for her eggs.
 
• C: Each stitch is neat and precise so that the leaf can be prevented from ripping.
 
 

Correct Sequence__: *ADBC*

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Parents are spending less time with their children.

options.text: Less time are being spent by parents with their children
Less time is spent by parents with their children
Less time is being spent by parents with their children
Less time is spending by parents with their children

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Less time is being spent by parents with their children'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the **active** voice and '**Parents**' is the subject and '**less time**' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject '**Parents**' of the **active** voice becomes the object, the object 'Less time' becomes the subject 
 
• The active format "are + Vᵢₙg" should be converted into the active format **"is/are/am + being** + V₃".
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the present continuous tense.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Kartik finally broke the high jump record.

options.text: The high jump record was finally broke by Kartik.
The high jump record is finally broken by Kartik.
The high jump record was finally broken by Kartik.
The high jump record finally broken by Kartik.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****The high jump record was finally broken by Kartik.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d75abffb1d7f21a0cb21fc40907655c03b3b6a401e1a3b03d94c609e009dc398.png] 

 
• In the given question the sentence 'The Smiths celebrated Christmas this year' is in **'Active voice'** which is in the **past indefinite** and we know that after converted this sentence into **'Passive voice'** the tense will same which also should in **past indefinite.**

 
 
• *Example: Reema **cleaned **the floor **(Active)**

 ​ ​The floor **was cleaned** by Reema **(Passive)***
 
 
 
• **Past indefinite structure: **
 
 
• Sub + V₂ + object **(Active)**

 ​Object + was/were + V₃ + by + subject** (Passive)**
 
 
 
• ***Hence the correct answer is-**** The high jump record was finally broken by Kartik.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a6a8f06b262806456af665e1b8217ceb8113d6bb49456f9395913c6248cabbdd.png] *

 
 

 **TENSE**
 **ACTIVE**
 **PASSIVE**
 
 

 **Past indefinite**
 Subject + V₂+ object
 Object+ was/were V₃+ by + subject
 
 

 **Past continuous**
 Subject + was/were + v₁+ing+ object.
 Object+ was/were +being+V₃+ by + subject
 
 

 **Past perfect**
 Subject + had + V₃+ object.
 Object+ had+been +V₃+ by + subject

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The maid said, "Shall I open the door?"

options.text: The maid asked if she shall open the door.
The maid asked if I should open the door.
The maid asked if she should open the door.
The maid said she should open the door.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

The given sentence is in Direct speech. It is an Interrogative sentence.

While converting from direct to Indirect speech, it is changed in an assertive statement.

__
 
• **Comma** and **inverted commas** are replaced by the verb '**ask**' **in past tense**. While reporting questions, the Indirect Speech is introduced by some verbs as 'asked', 'inquired', etc.
 
• The personal pronoun '**I**' is replaced with '**she**'.
 
• Also, the actual words have been spoken by the speaker in the past, therefore narrating it in the present will require a change in the tense.
 
• **The question mark** is replaced with a **full stop.**

**When we convert a sentence from direct to indirect speech, we make the following changes:__**

 
• **Quotation marks** are **omitted** and the sentence** ends with a full stop**. 
 
• The **tense** of the **verb**, in the reported speech involving any **order, request and instruction** does** not undergo** any **change **during the conversion from direct to indirect mode. This is also true if the statement is a** universal truth.** 
 
• If the** reporting verb** is in the **present tense**, it does **not undergo** any **change**.
 
• We add the word** 'to' **before the verb if the verb is in **bare infinitive**.
 
• When the reporting or **principal verb** is in the **present tense**, all present tenses of the direct are **changed** into the corresponding** past tenses.**
 
• Words expressing **nearness in time or place** are generally converted into into words expressing** distance**. For eg.** now** becomes **then**,** today** becomes **that day**, **yesterday** becomes **the previous day**, **this** becomes** that** etc.
 
• In reporting **commands and requests**, the** verb expressing command or request** is **added** and the** imperative **is changed into the** infinitive.** 
 
• In reporting** questions** the** verbs like asked, inquired** are **added** 
 
• In reporting** exclamations and wishes**, the** verbs expressing exclamation or wish** are **added**. 
 
• When we convert a sentence from the direct to the indirect mode(especially for a sentence** ending** with a** mark of interrogation**), we** reverse** the **subject-verb placement.** In **direct** sentences, we have the **verb before the subject**; while in** indirect,** the **verb follows the subject. **

Thus the correct sentence will be: *The maid asked if she should open the door.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

Banaras was visited by us on the occasion of Deepawali.

options.text: We had visited Banaras on the occasion of Deepawali.
We visited Banaras on the occasion of Deepawali
We visited Deepawali on the occasion of Banaras.
We are visiting Banaras on the occasion of Deepawali.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**We visited Banaras on the occasion of Deepawali**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We need to follow these instructions while changing the voice of an assertive sentence-

 
 
• Find the subject and object of the sentence and exchange their places; make changes in their cases as well if subject and object are pronouns.
 
• The proposition 'by' is removed in the active voice.
 
• If 'was/were + v3' (was visited) is used in the passive voice, the sentence in the active voice will be in the past indefinite tense. (visited)

 
 
 

The final sentence-* We visited Banaras on the occasion of Deepawali*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• The past indefinite tense is used to indicate a completed action that occurred at a specific point in time in the past.
 
• In the past indefinite tense the second form of the verb is used.
 
 
• E.g. Haryana government announced a complete lockdown in Gurgaon.

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

Were any questions asked about me by anyone?

options.text: Was anyone asking any questions about me?
Did anyone asked any questions about me?
Did anyone was asking any questions about me?
Did anyone ask any questions about me?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4.**

The sentence is in Passive voice and needs to be changed into an active voice.

__**Rules of Conversion from Passive to **Active **Voice:**__

 
• The subject of the active voice changes to object in the passive voice and vice versa
 
• Verb past tense '**were**' replaced with '**did'**
 
• Did + subject + was/were + object

Thus the correct sentence order we get is: *Did anyone ask any questions about me?*
